title: Marlowe & Finch Alterations Complimentary Basic Work: Conditions and Purchase Window
content:
Marlowe & Finch Alterations makes basic operations complimentary on garments bought at Marlowe & Finch on the terms below. A complimentary operation is recorded on the ticket as a complimentary basic waiver. Clauses marked as no longer in force are kept for the record with the limits of their retirement.

## 1. Conditions (all must hold)

(a) The class's complimentary basic work figure is "yes".

(b) > The ticket names a Marlowe & Finch purchase record in the customer's own name whose price type is one of the class's complimentary price types (sale, clearance, doorbuster and final sale items are charged; sale-priced items are not complimentary).

For a complimentary waiver that customer care books on a ticket, condition (b) is **no longer in force** as written; it is superseded by the current complimentary-work terms. For such a waiver the ticket must still name a Marlowe & Finch purchase record in the customer's own name, a regular-price purchase still has the operation waived in full, sale-price purchases are treated under those terms, and clearance, doorbuster and final sale purchases stay charged. Every other waiver remains under condition (b).

(c) The operation is one of the class's complimentary operations.

## 2. Purchase window

> The garment is dropped off within the complimentary window after the purchase's completed date.

For a complimentary waiver that customer care books on a ticket, this window sentence is **no longer in force**; the window for such a waiver is set by the current complimentary-work terms. Every other complimentary window remains under it.

The counting rule stays in force: the window counts calendar days starting the day after the purchase's completed date as day 1, and a drop-off on the last day of the class's purchase-window days is in time. The completed date is read from the purchase record the ticket names, and the drop-off date from the ticket — system records, not the customer's recollection.

| Hypothetical case (window of 60 days) | Day count | In time |
|---|---|---|
| Purchase completed on a given day; drop-off the next day | day 1 | yes |
| Drop-off on the 60th day after the completed date | day 60 | yes (last day) |
| Drop-off on the 61st day after the completed date | day 61 | no |

## 3. How many operations

> At most the class's maximum complimentary operations are complimentary (counted per purchase record across tickets), taken from the qualifying operations with the highest price first.

For a complimentary waiver that customer care books on a ticket, this sentence is **no longer in force**; the allowance for such a waiver is counted on the ticket under the current complimentary-work terms, and any further qualifying operation on that ticket stays chargeable. Every other complimentary waiver remains under this sentence.

## 4. What a complimentary operation covers

> Lined surcharges on a complimentary operation are complimentary too; rush fees and extra fittings never are.

For the complimentary waiver that customer care books, this sentence is **no longer in force**: that waiver covers the operation charge only, the lined surcharge of the operation stays chargeable whether the operation is waived in full or in part, and rush fees and extra fittings are never complimentary. Every other complimentary waiver remains under this sentence.

## 5. Gifts

A gift with a gift receipt counts as the recipient's purchase only when the purchase record is in the recipient's name.
